newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa suffers head injury after fall.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa suffers head injury after fall.

text.p: Mother Teresa was admitted to intensive care on Monday after she suffered a head injury in a fall, but doctors said her condition was not serious.

The 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun was taken to the intensive cardiac care unit of Calcutta's Woodlands Nursing Home after she fell at Mother House, headquarters of her Missionaries of Charity religious order.
"Mother Teresa had a fall this morning and sustained a minor injury in her head," the nursing home said in a statement. "Her condition is not serious".

"She doesn't have any temperature but her cardiac irregularity continues," the statement said, referring to the irregular heart beat which she has suffered since spending 18 days in hospital in late August and early September.
It said doctors carried out a a brain scan and results were expected early on Tuesday.
Mother Teresa, known as the Saint of the Gutters for her devotion to the poor and destitute, was in the same hospital between August 20 and September 6 with heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.
She spent most of the time on a respirator and was advised to rest in bed after being released.
Mother Teresa, who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979, was fitted with a cardiac pacemaker in 1989.
In 1991, she was treated at a Californian hospital for heart disease and bacterial pneumonia. Two years later she fell in Rome and broke three ribs.
In August 1993, she developed malaria, complicated by heart and lung problems. Last April she fractured her left collar bone.
The Missionaries of Charity, which she founded in 1949, runs some 544 homes for unwanted children and the destitute in more than 80 cities.
The work includes caring for nearly 7,000 children in 120 homes and arranging 1,500 adoptions each year.
